data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Topical immunomodulators & antipsoriatics_

**Class:** Topical calcineurin inhibitor (ascomycin macrolactam)

## Mechanism of action
- Binds macrophilin-12 (FKBP-12); complex inhibits calcineurin → blocks NFAT → reduces T-cell cytokines and mast cell mediator release
- More lipophilic and lower systemic absorption than tacrolimus; weaker effect (similar to low-potency steroid)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Mild–moderate atopic dermatitis (≥2 years; approved) — face, eyelids, flexures
- Seborrhoeic dermatitis, vitiligo (face), intertriginous psoriasis, perioral dermatitis, steroid rosacea

## Dose & formulations
- Twice daily; maintenance twice weekly

## Adverse effects
- Application-site burning/warmth (less than tacrolimus), skin infections (herpes, molluscum), alcohol flushing
- FDA boxed warning (theoretical malignancy) as for tacrolimus

## Contraindications
- Under 2 years (label), immunosuppression, Netherton syndrome, active infection at site

## Pregnancy & lactation
Minimal absorption; limited areas acceptable.

## Viva points
- Cream (pimecrolimus) vs ointment (tacrolimus); pimecrolimus is weaker and for mild disease

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.48; Khopkar ch.23. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
